claims.claim: Kao and Hockham proposed in 1965 that attenuation in optical fibers was caused by removable impurities rather than fundamental physics, making ultra-pure silica glass the right medium.
claims.episode_span: The answer required glass so free of impurities that a pulse could cross tens of kilometers before fading below detection.
claims.supporting_quote: They proposed that the attenuation in fibers available at the time was caused by impurities that could be removed, rather than by fundamental physical effects such as scattering.

claims.claim: Silica fiber attenuation fell about four orders of magnitude, from ~1000 dB/km in 1965 to ~0.17 dB/km in 2005.
claims.episode_span: driving attenuation from hundreds of decibels per kilometer down to fractions of a decibel
claims.supporting_quote: a four-order-of-magnitude reduction in the attenuation of silica optical fibers over four decades from ~1000 dB/km in 1965 to ~0.17 dB/km in 2005

claims.claim: Fiber preforms are made by vapor deposition in which silicon tetrachloride is reacted with oxygen inside a rotating glass tube.
claims.episode_span: engineers created a preform by reacting silicon tetrachloride and oxygen inside a rotating tube
claims.supporting_quote: the preform starts as a hollow glass tube approximately 40 centimeters (16 in) long, which is placed horizontally and rotated slowly on a lathe . Gases such as silicon tetrachloride (SiCl 4 ) or germanium tetrachloride (GeCl 4 ) are injected with oxygen in the end of the tube.

claims.claim: Long-haul fiber links require repeaters/amplifiers roughly every 70-150 km, consistent with the digest's 80-100 km amplifier spacing.
claims.episode_span: the optical amplifiers still required every eighty to one hundred kilometers
claims.supporting_quote: leading to long-haul fiber connections with repeater distances of 70–150 kilometers (43–93 mi)

claims.claim: The skin effect concentrates alternating current near the surface of a conductor, limiting copper at higher frequencies.
claims.episode_span: The skin effect concentrated current near the conductor surface at higher frequencies
claims.supporting_quote: skin effect is the tendency of an alternating electric current (AC) to become distributed within a conductor such that the current density is largest near the surface of the conductor
